description: West Virginia 211 helps residents find community services and understand provider intake requirements. Call, text your ZIP code or search its online resource database.
introduction: West Virginia 211 helps residents find community services and understand provider intake requirements. Call, text your ZIP code or search its online resource database.

who: People looking for West Virginia health and human services.
A referral does not establish eligibility for the provider’s benefit or service.
sections.get: Contact information, service descriptions, intake requirements and provider hours, including disaster-related resources.
sections.docs: Prepare your town or ZIP code, the type of help needed and any shutoff, housing or other urgent deadline. You can start requesting information without assembling a benefits document packet.
sections.apply:
1. Dial 211 or text your ZIP code to 898-211.
  2. If Wi-Fi calling or a VoIP phone will not connect, call 833-848-9905.
  3. Alternatively use Get Help on the WV 211 website to search resources.
  4. Contact the provider listed to start its intake process.
sections.after: Record the provider name and next step. Confirm availability directly because a listing does not reserve funds or an appointment. If the referral does not fit, explain the issue to a resource specialist and ask for alternatives.
sections.sources:
• WV 211 contact options
  • WV 211 resource database description
  • USA Assistance background and screenshots

faqs: What if 211 does not work on Wi-Fi calling?
No, contact DoHS for benefit eligibility and case decisions.
Does the database include application requirements?
WV 211 says its database includes intake requirements, eligibility and operating hours.
Can I look up services myself?
Use the Get Help database linked from its site.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
